42853990.text: A 5-year-old boy with high-risk neuroblastoma underwent 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT as part of a clinical trial to assess treatment response after anti-GD2 immunotherapy. The scan showed symmetric increased uptake in bilateral femora and tibiae with periostosis. 18F-MFBG PET/CT revealed no abnormal uptake, and no metastasis was found. The diagnosis was hypertrophic osteoarthropathy. This case demonstrates that hypertrophic osteoarthropathy can occur as a rare complication after anti-GD2 therapy and can be detected by 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.

42867540.label: Purpose
42867540.text: To evaluate whether pretreatment CT radiomics adds information for overall survival (OS) prediction among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), and assess frozen imaging-model performance in an independent cohort.

42867540.label: Methods
42867540.text: This retrospective study included 221 WAW-TACE and 98 HCC-TACE-SEG patients with pretreatment arterial and portal venous CT. Incremental value of a tumor-radiomics Random Survival Forest score (R1) beyond cohort-specific clinical Cox models (C0) was evaluated within each cohort using 5-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times. External validation was restricted to frozen WAW-trained R1 models (Top-K = 5, 10, 15) applied to HCC-TACE-SEG without refitting; the combined C0 + R1 model was not externally validated.

42867540.label: Results
42867540.text: WAW-TACE included 162 deaths and HCC-TACE-SEG 86 deaths. In WAW-TACE, C0, R1 Top-K = 15, and C0 + R1 achieved C-indices of 0.646 ± 0.043, 0.593 ± 0.049, and 0.639 ± 0.045, respectively. Corresponding HCC-TACE-SEG estimates were 0.496 ± 0.087, 0.530 ± 0.072, and 0.495 ± 0.094. Thus, R1 did not consistently improve cohort-specific clinical reference models. In frozen external application, Top-K = 5, 10, and 15 achieved C-indices of 0.463 (95% CI 0.397-0.532), 0.535 (0.468-0.608), and 0.528 (0.460-0.598), respectively.

42867540.label: Conclusion
42867540.text: The evaluated models showed no consistent incremental value for OS prediction within these TACE cohorts and limited frozen-model discrimination in the clinically distinct HCC-TACE-SEG cohort. These findings do not support clinical use of these models or establish a general limitation of CT radiomics.

42886040.text: Purpose To compare the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of three MRI protocols for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) according to prebiopsy risk. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included 390 male patients who underwent prostate multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) between January 2019 and April 2024 for suspected csPCa, followed by biopsy. Patients were stratified by Rotterdam Prostate Cancer Risk Calculator score into low-risk (<4%), intermediate-risk (4%-9%), and high-risk (≥10%) groups. Three datasets were generated from each examination: mpMRI (T2-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging [DWI], and dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging), unenhanced MRI (multiplanar T2-weighted imaging and DWI), and short MRI (axial T2-weighted imaging and DWI). Overall, 1170 datasets were randomly assigned to 10 expert radiologists (117 examinations each). Diagnostic performance for grade group 2 or greater cancer and clinical utility metrics were compared across risk groups. Results Among the 390 patients (median age, 66 years [IQR, 61-71 years]), csPCa prevalence was 34.4% (134 of 390). In low-risk patients, short MRI demonstrated the highest sensitivity (95% [21 of 22]), with no significant differences among protocols (all P ≥ .21) and greatest potential for safe biopsy avoidance (84 biopsies avoided per missed csPCa). In intermediate-risk patients, mpMRI showed higher sensitivity (83% vs 72% for unenhanced MRI and 62% for short MRI; P = .012 for mpMRI vs short MRI) and higher biopsy efficiency (1.11 vs 0.85 for mpMRI vs unenhanced MRI). In high-risk patients, protocol-related differences were minimal (all P ≥ .12). Conclusion mpMRI was associated with improved sensitivity and biopsy efficiency in intermediate-risk patients, whereas protocol differences were limited in low- and high-risk groups; these findings support risk-adapted selection of MRI protocols.

42912540.text: We present [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT findings of an incidentally detected benign phyllodes tumor in a 68-year-old woman with prior colon cancer. Routine contrast-enhanced CT revealed a right breast nodule with moderate enhancement, and subsequent PET/CT demonstrated intense focal FAPI uptake (SUVmax: 6.63). Histology confirmed the presence of a benign phyllodes tumor. This case highlights that FAPI-avid lesions in cancer survivors may represent benign entities with fibroblast-rich stroma, underscoring the importance of considering benign diagnoses and obtaining histologic confirmation to avoid unnecessary treatment.

42955840.text: Vascular abnormalities are less common in the hand and wrist than in the lower extremities but can result in significant morbidity if unrecognized or untreated. The unique vascular architecture of the hand and wrist, with a dense network of arterial anastomoses, confers resilience to ischemia, but the superficial location makes them vulnerable to trauma and occupational injury. The authors describe and illustrate a comprehensive multimodality imaging approach to the diagnosis and evaluation of vascular abnormalities of the hand and wrist. They begin with an overview of vascular anatomy and normal variants, including a persistent median artery. Multimodality imaging, including US, CT angiography, MR angiography, and digital subtraction angiography, is reviewed with a focus on strengths, limitations, and clinical utility. Dynamic imaging techniques and photon-counting CT are highlighted for their evolving roles. A wide spectrum of vascular diseases, including atherosclerosis, trauma, iatrogenic injury, embolism, hypothenar hammer syndrome, hand-arm vibration syndrome, vasculitis, and frostbite, as well as their imaging appearances, are discussed. Vascular anomalies, including vascular malformations and vascular neoplasms, are also reviewed. The role of imaging in hand transplantation is addressed. The authors provide a framework for recognizing vascular diseases in the hand and wrist and selecting the appropriate imaging modality. Familiarity with vascular anatomy, imaging findings, and clinical context is essential for timely diagnosis, guiding management, and preserving limb function.

42965590.label: Background
42965590.text: Ki-67 expression is a valuable prognostic indicator in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA). This study aimed to develop a non-invasive Deep learning (DL) model based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and clinical data to predict Ki-67 expression preoperatively.

42965590.label: Methods
42965590.text: Patients with iCCA between January 2020 and January 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Based on immunohistochemistry, patients were classified into high-expression group (Ki-67 > 50%) and low-expression group (Ki-67 ≤ 50%). After image acquisition, tumor segmentation, and preprocessing, a 3D-ResNet10 network was utilized for MRI feature extraction. A feed-forward neural network (FFN) was used for clinical feature extraction. Subsequently, the extracted image and clinical features were fused and fed into a lightweight classifier to perform Ki-67 level prediction. The performance of the DL models was evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and the area under the curve (AUC).

42965590.label: Results
42965590.text: A total of 117 patients were ultimately included (30 cases in the high-expression group and 87 cases in the low-expression group). The model based solely on clinical variables demonstrated limited predictive efficacy (mean AUC: 53.18 ± 14.60%). The model utilizing MRI features alone exhibited high specificity (86.14 ± 10.25%) but modest sensitivity. In contrast, the fused DL model significantly outperformed both individual models, attaining a mean AUC of 84.24 ± 8.82%, an accuracy of 87.17 ± 5.95%, a specificity of 93.07 ± 9.35%, and a markedly improved sensitivity of 70.00 ± 19.44%, yielding a robust F1-score of 73.42 ± 12.28%.

42965590.label: Conclusions
42965590.text: We developed and validated a non-invasive DL model integrating contrast-enhanced MRI and clinical parameters that accurately predicts Ki-67 expression in iCCA, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance.

42967440.label: Purpose
42967440.text: To evaluate agreement of proposed CT-based variants with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in suspected advanced ovarian cancer and assess inter-reader agreement of CT-derived components.

42967440.label: Methods
42967440.text: This retrospective single-center study included consecutive adults evaluated between January 2021 and November 2025 for suspected advanced ovarian cancer who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT and staging laparoscopy. Proposed CT-based modifications were operationalized as six score variants combining CT-derived peritoneal tumor burden, CT-estimated ascites, cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), and either Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG-PS) or CT-derived body composition parameters. Agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Spearman correlation coefficient, and weighted Cohen's kappa.

42967440.label: Results
42967440.text: The final cohort included 80 patients. All CT-based variants showed agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. For the variant combining CT-derived PCI, CT-estimated ascites, ECOG-PS, and CA-125, the consistency ICC was 0.76, Spearman's ρ was 0.806, and weighted Cohen's kappa was 0.76. This variant showed 70.0% agreement across the three risk categories and 83.8% agreement for high-risk versus non-high-risk classification, classifying 20 of 22 laparoscopic high-risk patients as high risk. The PCI-based skeletal muscle index (SMI) variant maintained substantial agreement: ICC, 0.73; Spearman correlation coefficient, 0.742; weighted Cohen's kappa, 0.74. Inter-reader agreement was high for CT-derived PCI, with an ICC of 0.91.

42967440.label: Conclusion
42967440.text: Proposed CT-based variants showed agreement with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. The PCI-based ECOG-PS variant showed the highest agreement metrics, suggesting that structured CT assessment may help approximate laparoscopic risk categories before invasive evaluation.

42975390.label: Objective
42975390.text: To evaluate early facility performance on the CMS-adopted Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality for Diagnostic CT in Adults (ExRad) measure, the first automated radiology outcome measure in CMS payment programs, during the first 16 months of the measure's inclusion in CMS programs.

42975390.label: Methods
42975390.text: ExRad evaluates each adult diagnostic CT examination in three steps: assignment to 1 of 19 CT categories defined by anatomic region and clinical indication; computation of size-adjusted radiation dose and image noise from the DICOM radiation dose-structured report and pixel data; and comparison of both against category-specific thresholds. Because the clinical and radiology data sit in separate systems, translation software inside the health system firewall may be used to perform the linkage. An examination is out of range if its dose or noise exceeds its category threshold; a facility's score is the percentage of eligible examinations out of range (lower is better). We analyzed all facilities reporting between May 2025 and August 2026.

42975390.label: Results
42975390.text: Across 254 facilities and 783,634 examinations in 16 CT categories, 30.7% were out of range: 240,409 (30.7%) exceeded the dose threshold and 446 (0.06%) the noise threshold. Facility scores varied widely: median 29.5% (interquartile range [IQR] 18.4-44.7; range 1.8-82.4), with facilities at the 90th percentile scoring 4.6 times more out-of-range scans than those at the 10th percentile. Median out-of-range percentages by category ranged from 0% (routine and low-dose cardiac) to 82.6% (high-dose head; IQR 23.5-100.0); routine abdomen and pelvis, the highest-volume category, had a median of 43.9% (IQR 30.1-61.3). Within facilities, the median gap between best- and worst-performing category was 74 percentage points (IQR 49-89; intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.12).

42975390.label: Discussion
42975390.text: Early ExRad performance varied widely across facilities and across CT categories within the same facility. Most variation reflected particular facility-category combinations, so facilities need their own category-level results to identify which protocols to target.

42980990.label: Background
42980990.text: Postoperative staging and residual/metastatic lesion detection of papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) before radioiodine (RAI) ablation remains a critical clinical demand, especially for patients with intermediate to high-risk pathological features. Although 2-[18F] fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose ([18F] FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) is widely applied in thyroid cancer imaging, its diagnostic sensitivity is suboptimal for small-volume, low-metabolic metastatic or residual lesions. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP), specifically overexpressed in tumor stromal cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), has become a novel and reliable imaging target for oncological detection. This study aimed to head-to-head compare the diagnostic efficacy of [18F]AL-NOTA-FAPI-46 ([18F] FAPI-46) and [¹⁸F] FDG PET/CT in identifying postoperative residual and lymph node metastatic lesions in PTC patients prior to adjuvant ¹³¹I therapy.

42980990.label: Methods
42980990.text: A total of 18 consecutive postoperative PTC patients scheduled for ¹³¹I ablation were prospectively enrolled. All patients underwent paired [18F] FAPI-46 and [18F] FDG PET/CT within a 1-week interval before treatment. A composite reference standard integrating histopathological results, standardized imaging follow-up (median follow-up duration: 8 months, range: 6-12 months) and continuous clinical serological monitoring was adopted to verify lesion properties. Two experienced nuclear medicine physicians independently and blindly interpreted all PET/CT images in random order, with consensus arbitration for discrepant results. Quantitative imaging parameters including SUVmax and SUVpeak were calculated for all target lesions.

42980990.label: Results
42980990.text: For lymph node metastatic lesion detection, [18F] FAPI-46 PET/CT exhibited significantly higher sensitivity (82.3% vs. 29.4%, exact two-tailed P = 0.022) and accuracy (78.3% vs. 30.4%) than [18F] FDG PET/CT, with fewer false-positive cases (2 vs. 4). The true-positive lymph nodes showed significantly higher SUVmax (4.2 ± 3.2 vs. 1.6 ± 2.6, P = 0.015), SUVpeak (3.0 ± 2.1 vs. 1.0 ± 1.7, P = 0.005) on [18F] FAPI-46 imaging than [18F] FDG. Three false-positive bone lesions with increased [18F] FAPI-46 uptake was found in two patients. These lesions were confirmed as benign fibroproliferative lesions via CT morphological features and follow-up imaging, and no true bone metastasis was detected in the entire cohort. Patients with confirmed lymph node metastasis had significantly higher serum stimulated thyroglobulin (sTg) levels (79.1 ± 51.1 ng/mL vs. 33.9 ± 36.5 ng/mL, P = 0.044). The optimal sTg diagnostic threshold for metastatic lesion screening was 25.9 ng/mL (AUC = 0.862), while the predictive value of this cutoff needs further large-sample validation. All enrolled patients had negative anti-thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb) status(< 15ng/mL) to eliminate serological detection interference. [18F] FAPI-46 PET/CT successfully identified occult lymph node metastases in patients with elevated sTg and corrected the false-positive findings of [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT.

42980990.label: Conclusions
42980990.text: In this prospective pilot study, [18F] FAPI-46 PET/CT demonstrated superior diagnostic performance over [18F] FDG PET/CT for detecting postoperative lymph node metastatic lesions in PTC patients before RAI ablation, with better capability to distinguish malignant lesions from reactive lymph nodes.

43013090.label: Objectives
43013090.text: To derive a multi-organ imaging biomarker panel from whole-body MRI and evaluate its predictive value for incident type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), including the role of intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) in reconciling discrepancies between muscle volume and metabolic risk.

43013090.label: Materials and methods
43013090.text: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 46,129 UK Biobank participants without diabetes at the time of imaging. Organ volume indices and fat fractions were extracted from Dixon MRI through automated segmentation. Associations between muscle volume indices, fat fractions, and handgrip strength were evaluated, and IMAT was graded in strength-matched participants. Independent imaging biomarkers were identified using adjusted Cox models, and a deep learning model was trained. Added value relative to the Leicester risk assessment score was evaluated using decision curve analysis.

43013090.label: Results
43013090.text: During follow-up, 600 participants developed T2DM. Eight biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM, including liver volume index (hazard ratio (HR), 1.28; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.19-1.38), pancreas fat fraction (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.10-1.28), and gluteus fat fraction (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.08-1.27). Gluteal IMAT grades were higher in weak-for-volume participants than in strength-matched controls (median, 2.0 vs 1.0; p = 0.02). The deep learning model achieved a concordance index of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.797-0.832) and, when applied sequentially with clinical criteria, reduced false-positive classifications by 43.0% while preserving 97.3% of true positives.

43013090.label: Conclusion
43013090.text: Whole-body MRI-derived multi-organ biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM and enhanced risk stratification beyond an established clinical risk score. Muscle fat fraction may better reflect metabolic risk than muscle volume in IMAT-rich regions.

43013090.label: Key points
43013090.text: Question Clinical risk scores miss the multi-organ pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes; does whole-body MRI organ size and fat quantification improve prediction of incident diabetes? Findings Eight MRI-derived biomarkers independently predicted incident type 2 diabetes; a deep learning model using whole-body MRI biomarkers reached a concordance index of 0.814. Clinical relevance Automated whole-body MRI biomarkers capture multi-organ metabolic signatures beyond conventional risk scoring. Applied after clinical screening, they remove 43.0% of false-positive classifications while preserving 97.3% of true positives.

43037690.label: Purpose
43037690.text: To evaluate whether MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers are associated with clinical severity and prognosis in chronic liver disease (CLD).

43037690.label: Materials and methods
43037690.text: In this retrospective single-center study, 165 adults with chronic liver disease (CLD) who underwent gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI were included. Functional Liver Imaging Score (FLIS) was assessed on 20-min hepatobiliary-phase images, and Liver Surface Nodularity (LSN) was measured on contrast-enhanced axial T1-weighted images using semi-automated software. Spearman correlation analysis was performed for associations with Model for End-Stage Liver Disease 3.0 (MELD 3.0), and Albumin-Bilirubin score (ALBI). Time-to-event analyses for liver transplantation or death within 4 years were performed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the performance of FLIS for predicting 1-year transplant-free survival (TFS).

43037690.label: Results
43037690.text: FLIS showed moderate inverse correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = - 0.532, p < 0.001) and ALBI score (ρ = - 0.541, p < 0.001). LSN showed weak positive correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = 0.154, p = 0.049) and ALBI score (ρ = 0.184, p = 0.018). In univariable Cox analysis, older age, lower FLIS, higher MELD 3.0, higher ALBI score, and LSN cutoff ≥ 3 were associated with a higher risk of liver transplantation/death. In multivariable analysis, age (hazard ratio (HR), 1.05; p < 0.001), MELD 3.0 (HR, 1.08; p = 0.003) and FLIS group (0-3 vs 4-6 points; HR, 2.39; p = 0.007) remained independently associated with liver transplantation or death. For 1-year TFS, FLIS with an optimal cutoff of ≤ 3 yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.71 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.82).

43037690.label: Conclusion
43037690.text: Our findings suggest that MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers, particularly FLIS, may provide noninvasive imaging markers of disease severity and prognosis in patients with CLD. Prospective studies with long-term clinical outcomes are needed to define their role in risk stratification and transplant decision-making.

43079090.label: Purpose
43079090.text: To develop and validate an integrated PET/CT‑based radiomic model that combines tumour characteristics and whole‑body composition features for predicting progression‑free survival (PFS) in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).

43079090.label: Methods
43079090.text: This multicentre retrospective study included 477 patients with pathologically confirmed ESCC who underwent pretreatment [¹⁸F]FDG‑PET/CT. Patients were allocated to training (n = 294), internal validation (n = 74), and external validation (n = 109) cohorts. Primary tumours and whole‑body composition components, including skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, intermuscular adipose tissue and spine, were automatically segmented on PET/CT images. Radiomic features were extracted from both tumour and body‑composition regions. Feature selection and model development were performed using machine learning approaches. A composite clinical-tumour-body composition model was constructed and compared with clinical and tumour‑radiomic models.

43079090.label: Results
43079090.text: The integrated model showed superior prognostic performance over individual models, achieving C‑indices of 0.802 (95% CI: 0.770-0.832), 0.716 (95% CI: 0.639-0.797), and 0.732 (95% CI: 0.660-0.796) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. The corresponding AUCs for 3‑year PFS prediction were 0.895 (95% CI: 0.858-0.930), 0.831 (95% CI: 0.727-0.923), and 0.772 (95% CI: 0.639-0.895). The model stratified patients into high‑ and low‑risk groups, with significantly different PFS between the two strata across all cohorts (log‑rank P < 0.05). Decision curve analysis supported the clinical utility of the integrated model.

43079090.label: Conclusions
43079090.text: A PET/CT‑based radiomic model integrating clinical, tumour, and whole‑body composition features provides robust, externally validated postoperative prognostic stratification for ESCC. This approach may facilitate individualised risk assessment and inform treatment decision‑making.
